suggestions.quote: Each chip is one person's chance at the one thing they'd choose... with nobody watching. It never tells you what that thing is.
suggestions.fix: Replace the last sentence with: “At first, it doesn't tell you what that thing is.” This avoids contradicting the later goal labels.

suggestions.quote: > HOLD: 2.5 s. Montage, under a second each: you pour tea onto your own shoe; you count change wrong; you nap on a sack of tea leaves. Above, in the coaching centre's lit window, the batch goes on without you.
suggestions.fix: Replace one generic stall gag with a premise-specific failure: you copy the chaiwala's exact wrist flick, the tea misses the cup, his chip rises and yours falls.

suggestions.quote: > SCENE: The last bus home, your forehead against the window. Outside, the city passes, and over every head in it a chip: thousands, flickering, each one changing as its person moves.
suggestions.fix: Establish the chronology without changing the owner-approved narration: “The next night after class: the last bus home, your forehead against the window...”

keep.quote: You can't borrow someone's odds. Only their apron.
The biggest number? It tells you what's likely. It can't tell you what's worth choosing.
But it's his. And it's moving.
